task: Implement the FINIX 'Srishti Math' spec gaps by replacing hardcoded/stub handler responses with real deterministic domain logic, and by hardening the transaction risk score.

context.layout_convention: Pure, testable math lives in internal/domain/<name>/ (see existing internal/domain/{transaction,healthscore,fraud}). Service layer (internal/domain/platform) orchestrates and holds state; handlers in service_expansion.go / router.go return JSON.
context.money_convention: All monetary values are int64 paise. 1 rupee = 100 paise. Never use float for money storage; float is acceptable only for intermediate rate math, round back to int64 paise.
context.guiding_principle: The spec's thesis is that these numbers must be mathematically real and reproducible for RBI model-risk audit, not illustrative. No approximations where a full simulation is feasible. Every threshold/weight/rate must be versioned config, not a magic literal.

global_instructions: Create new domain packages as pure functions with no I/O and no mutexes; unit-test each formula with table-driven tests.
Replace map[string]any{...} literals in handlers with calls into the new domain packages.
Do not change existing route paths or JSON field names that the Flutter client consumes; add fields, don't rename.
Run gofmt, go vet, and golangci-lint; add tests and ensure `go test ./...` passes before considering an item done.
Where a value is currently a magic literal (risk tiers 40/70, cooling-off 6h, foreclosure 0.08/0.015, meanGrowth 0.07, stdDev 0.12), source it from a versioned ModelParams config struct instead.
Preserve XAI explanation strings but make them reflect the computed numbers, not canned text.

prompts.title: Debt Optimisation Engine — core amortisation primitives
requirements: EMI(principalPaise int64, annualRatePct float64, months int) int64 using EMI = P·r·(1+r)^n/((1+r)^n − 1), r = annualRatePct/12/100. Handle r==0 (return P/n) and months<=0 (error or 0).

Schedule(principalPaise int64, annualRatePct float64, months int) []Row where Row{Month int; InterestPaise, PrincipalPaise, BalancePaise int64}; simulate the full table, InterestComponent(k)=Balance(k-1)·r, PrincipalComponent(k)=EMI−Interest, Balance(k)=Balance(k-1)−Principal.
TotalInterest(rows []Row) int64 summing the schedule (do NOT approximate).
SolveTenure(principalPaise int64, annualRatePct float64, emiPaise int64) int for floating-rate tenure recompute: n = -ln(1 - P·r/EMI)/ln(1+r).
Round money to int64 paise at each step; final row balance must reach ~0.
tests: Known EMI: 10,00,000 principal at 9% for 60 months ≈ ₹20,758/mo (verify against a standard EMI calculator).
Sum of PrincipalPaise across schedule == original principal (±rounding).
r==0 edge case; single-month loan; zero principal.

prompts.title: Debt Optimisation Engine — prepayment, foreclosure, avalanche/snowball, repo recompute
requirements: PrepaymentImpact(loan, extraPaise, extraMonth): run Schedule twice (baseline vs. balance reduced by extra at extraMonth, re-amortised at same EMI); return InterestSavedPaise = TotalInterest(base)−TotalInterest(prepay) and TenureReducedMonths = len(base)−len(prepay). Replaces the current `extra*14` and `11` literals.

ForeclosurePenaltyRate(loanType string, floating bool) float64: MUST return 0 for floating-rate individual retail loans per RBI 2014 circular (this is a compliance correctness fix — current code hardcodes has_penalty:true which is wrong). Fixed-rate/business loans use a versioned lender rate.

ForeclosureDecision: NetBenefit = RemainingInterestIfHeld − PenaltyAmount − OpportunityCost, where OpportunityCost = amountUsed × (expectedInvestmentReturn − loanRate) × remainingYears. Flag 'not recommended' when NetBenefit < 0. XAI must show the opportunity-cost term explicitly, not just penalty-vs-savings.

OptimiseStrategy(loans []Loan, extraTarget int64, adherenceScore float64): simulate avalanche (sort by rate desc) and snowball (sort by balance asc) waterfalls; return both total-interest numbers, InterestCostOfSnowball = avalanche−snowball (always ≥0), and RecommendedStrategy per §4.3 rule (Avalanche unless documented low adherence). XAI must show BOTH numbers regardless of recommendation.
RepoRateRecompute(loan, deltaRepoBps float64, transmissionFactor float64): newRate = oldRate + deltaRepoBps/10000·transmissionFactor; recompute EMI via P1. Replaces hardcoded 2915000.
ExpectedInvestmentReturn and transmissionFactor come from versioned config.
tests: Snowball total interest ≥ avalanche total interest (never worse).
Floating individual loan → penalty == 0; fixed loan → penalty > 0.
Foreclosure with loan rate below expected return → NetBenefit negative (not recommended) even with zero penalty.
Prepayment reduces tenure, not EMI, by default.

prompts.title: Credit Utilisation & BNPL EffectiveAPR
prompts.replace_stubs_in: service_expansion.go handleLoanEndpoints (loan_credit_utilisation returns constant 0.27; loan_bnpl returns hardcoded LazyPay)
requirements: Utilisation(outstandingPaise, limitPaise int64) float64 per card; AggregateUtilisation(cards) = Σoutstanding/Σlimit. Surface BOTH per-card and aggregate (a maxed single card is hidden by aggregate).
Alert when a card crosses 0.30 BEFORE statement date; implement T-5-day lead-time check against statement_date.
EffectiveAPR(totalRepayablePaise, principalPaise int64, tenureDays int) float64 = ((totalRepayable/principal) − 1) × (365/tenureDays). Show side-by-side with the headline (often '0%') rate.
IsBNPLObligation(mcc string, counterparty string) bool via MCC set + provider-name registry (versioned config).
Expose a helper so BNPL principal outstanding is included in TotalDebt for the health-score DTI (P6) and debt engine (P2).
tests: 0.30 threshold boundary; aggregate-fine-but-one-card-maxed case.
EffectiveAPR of a '0% headline' BNPL with fees materially > 0.
T-5 alert fires before statement date, not after.

prompts.title: Transaction risk score — unit/denominator safety (clipping + floors)
requirements: This is the spec's #1 'security-relevant bug' concern: unclipped ratios cause NaN/Inf and silent false-HIGH/false-LOW.
Clip AmountVsAverage to [0,25] and BalanceImpact to [0,1] before weighting (add a normalise step in signalToFeatures or at top of assess()).
Floor denominators where the ratios are computed upstream: user_avg_amount uses FLOOR_AVG = ₹500 (50000 paise); balance denominator floored at 1 paise.
Apply g(x)=clip((x−1)·k_amt, 0, cap_amt) form for the amount term with versioned k_amt/cap_amt.
Guard against NaN/Inf explicitly (if math.IsNaN/IsInf → treat as max-anomalous or safe default per spec intent).
tests: New-account (zero history) input does not produce NaN/Inf and yields a bounded score.
AmountVsAverage of 1000x clips to the 25x ceiling.
BalanceImpact > 1 clips to 1.

prompts.title: Transaction risk score — geo (impossible-travel), day-of-week, market-context terms
requirements: Add RiskSignal fields: DistanceKm, HoursSinceLastTxn float64; Country, HomeCountry string; HasInternationalHistory bool; DowZScore float64; VolIndexPercentile float64.
geo_term: Haversine(lat1,lon1,lat2,lon2); impossible_travel if distance/hours > 900 km/h → 25; else 10 if country != home_country AND no international history; else 0.
dow_term = clip(5·max(0, z_dow − 1.5), 0, 10); require ≥4 same-weekday observations before trusting (else 0) — the caller supplies the z-score and observation count.
market_context_term = 8 if (AmountVsAverage > 3 AND vol_index_t > 90th-percentile) else 0.
All weights and thresholds (900 km/h, 1.5, 3, p90) from versioned config.
tests: Two logged-in sessions 5000km apart within 1h → impossible-travel flag, geo_term 25.
First-ever international txn with no history → geo_term 10.
dow_term is 0 when fewer than 4 weekday observations.

prompts.title: AML structuring/smurfing control
prompts.reason_not_contained: Needs recent transaction history, so it lives in the service layer, not the pure heuristic.
requirements: StructuringFlag(userID, window=24h): count(txns to NEW recipients) ≥ 3 AND Σamount > 0.9×SingleTxnStructuringBenchmark AND stdev(amounts) < 0.15×mean(amounts) (suspiciously uniform).
When flagged, force MEDIUM tier minimum regardless of per-transaction scores, with its own XAI reason ('several similarly-sized payments to new recipients in a short window').
Benchmark and thresholds from versioned config (PMLA-aligned).
tests: 3 uniform payments to new recipients in 24h → forced MEDIUM.
3 payments with high variance in amounts → not flagged.
2 payments (below count threshold) → not flagged.

prompts.title: P_high-proportional cooling-off and friction
requirements: cooling_off_minutes(P_high) = base_cooloff_minutes × (1 + κ·(P_high − 0.70)), base = 240 min (4h per spec), κ ≈ 2, HIGH tier only.
override_friction_level = base_friction + λ·max(0, P_high − 0.70), λ > 0, HIGH tier only.
Thresholds/base/κ/λ from versioned config. Note current code uses a fixed 6h base that differs from the spec's 4h — align to spec base and make proportional.
Ensure VerifyCoolingOff and the middleware read the computed duration, not a constant.
tests: P_high=0.70 → cooling-off == base (240 min).
MEDIUM/LOW tier → no proportional escalation.

prompts.title: Monte Carlo simulation — honesty envelope & goal probability
requirements: Compute GoalCompletionProbability = count(C_T ≥ C_target)/N using the already-sorted results; round to nearest 1% (no false precision like 73.482%).
Replace hardcoded GoalCompletionDeltaPct: 6.4 and keyword-based HealthScoreDelta with computed values.

Add Assumptions metadata to every result: {SimulationCount N, Mu, Sigma, Blend, HistoricalWindowYears, Disclaimer:'based on historical patterns, not a prediction or guarantee of future returns'} — maps to spec S22.5 disclaimer set.

Preferred: replace flat Normal(0.07,0.12) with bootstrap resampling from a historical returns slice (≥10y NSE/AMFI category history) — spec calls the Normal assumption less defensible given fat tails. If historical data unavailable, keep Normal but document it in Assumptions.blend.
Keep P10/P50/P90 fan-chart percentiles (already present).
tests: Probability is in [0,1] and rounded to whole percent.
Assumptions block is populated and disclaimer present.
Deterministic seed → reproducible percentiles for audit.

prompts.title: Financial Health Score — fill undefined pillar functions + audit snapshot
prompts.modify: internal/domain/healthscore/calculator.go (+ new inputs); add snapshot schema in repo layer
requirements: CoefficientOfVariation(series) = std/max(mean, FLOOR) with small positive FLOOR (job-loss month → large CV, not crash).
IdleCashMonths penalty = clip(8·(IdleCashMonths−3), 0, 40), soft not binary.

TargetCorpusForAge(age, income): YearsToRetirement=max(60−age,0); RequiredAnnualIncomeAtRetirement=0.70·income·(1+inflation)^years; TargetCorpus=Required·AnnuityFactor(25, 0.03) where AnnuityFactor(n,r)=(1−(1+r)^-n)/r. Versioned config for 60/0.70/25/0.03.
score_LoanMix = 40 + 60·GoodDebtRatio where GoodDebtRatio=(HomeLoan+EducationLoan)/TotalDebt.

Cold-start (§2.1): if months_of_history < 3 → use onboarding proxy from snapshot data only, trend/consistency sub-terms default to neutral 50; display 'Preliminary — based on limited history' badge; no EWMA. For 3–6 months, EWMA over available months, renormalise denominator, do NOT pad missing months with zeros.

Persist FinancialHealthSnapshot{userID, snapshotMonth, computedAt, P1..P7, RawComposite 300-900, inputHash (sha256 of feature vector for reproducibility), modelVersion, dataCompleteness 0-1}. Surface dataCompleteness in XAI ('score 656, but 40% estimated').
tests: Same inputHash → identical RawComposite (reproducibility).
Zero-income month → LOW CashFlowReg via large CV, no crash/NaN.
months_of_history<3 → neutral-50 sub-terms + preliminary flag.
dataCompleteness reflects fraction of real vs. defaulted sub-metrics.

prompts.title: Mule GNN structural features (fill patternScore fallback)
requirements: FanInRatio(v) = InDegree/max(OutDegree,1); FanOutBurstiness(v) = largest 24h outbound after large inbound / TotalInboundLast24h.
AccountAgeAtFirstLargeCredit < 24h flag (highest-precision new-mule signal).
ClusteringCoefficient(v) = 2·triangles/(deg·(deg−1)); LOW clustering among counterparties is mule-consistent.

CompositeStructuralScore(v) = sigmoid(a1·z(FanIn) + a2·z(FanOutBurst) + a3·1[age<24h] − a4·z(Clustering)); use as the non-hardcoded fallback for recipients with no path from any seed node, replacing the keyword/structural placeholder.
Coefficients a1..a4 from versioned config.
tests: Funnel pattern (many senders, one recipient) → high FanInRatio → elevated score.
New account receiving large credit within 24h → flag set.
Normal clustered social graph → low structural score.

prompts.title: Market Manipulation & Panic-Selling defence
prompts.reason_not_contained: Needs SMS-classifier output (Model 10) and SELL-order interception; new data dependencies.
requirements: Trigger_TipToTrade: flagged SMS/email (AMBER/RED) in preceding ~72h referencing order.instrument AND instrument avg_daily_volume < LowLiquidityThreshold → elevate market_context_term + XAI reason. Large-cap filter avoids false flags.
Trigger_PanicSell: SELL AND amount > 0.25·TotalEquityPortfolioValue AND intraday index drawdown ≤ −3% → surface calm-down prompt reusing Model-13 deterministic hold-vs-sell projection (NOT new math).

COMPLIANCE: both are informational/protective only — must NEVER block/delay a SELL beyond the already-reviewed S9.4A.4 cooling-off. Calm-down prompt one-tap dismissible; dismissal not logged as evidence against the user.
tests: SELL of 30% during −4% drawdown → calm-down prompt (dismissible), order still proceeds.
Spam SMS referencing a large-cap → not flagged (liquidity filter).
Prompt dismissal produces no adverse log entry.

prompts.title: News / Disinformation Integrity Filter
prompts.reason_not_contained: Needs an article feed and source registry; replaces canned marketNews/marketTrends.
requirements: Stage 1 — deterministic source whitelist (blockchain-anchored per S11A.6): admit only if source_domain ∈ ApprovedSourceWhitelist (BSE/NSE/RBI/SEBI + named versioned media list). Non-admitted articles are never shown. Whitelist changes require the multi-party consensus governance process, not a code change.

Stage 2 — DisinfoScore on whitelisted content only: w1·UrgencyLexiconDensity + w2·1[no attributable source in first 3 paragraphs] + w3·1[extreme/superlative density above outlet baseline] − w4·1[cites official filing]. Soft-flag 'review with caution' above calibrated threshold; NEVER hard-block a whitelisted source.
Weights and whitelist are versioned config.
tests: Non-whitelisted domain → never returned.
Whitelisted opinion piece with urgency lexicon → soft 'review with caution', still shown.
Article citing an official RBI filing → score reduced.

prompts.title: Versioned model parameters (cross-cutting)
requirements: Introduce a ModelParams struct with Version string and grouped fields: RiskTiers{Medium:40,High:70}, AmountTerm{K,Cap}, CoolingOff{BaseMinutes:240,Kappa:2,Lambda}, Geo{ImpossibleTravelKmh:900}, Simulation{Mu:0.07,Sigma:0.12,Blend,HistoricalYears}, Foreclosure{...}, HealthScore{RetirementAge:60,ReplacementRate:0.70,PostYears:25,RealReturn:0.03}, Structuring{Benchmark,MinCount:3}.
Load once at startup (env or embedded default), thread into domain constructors (RiskEngine, Calculator, debt/credit funcs).
Expose ModelParams.Version so it can be written into FinancialHealthSnapshot.modelVersion and simulation Assumptions.
Replace scattered magic literals (40/70, 6h, 0.08/0.015, 0.07/0.12) with reads from this struct.
tests: Default params load and validate.
Overriding a threshold via env changes the scoring output.
Version string propagates into snapshot and simulation metadata.

verification: go build ./... && go vet ./... && gofmt -l . (expect empty) && golangci-lint run ./...
go test ./... passes including new table tests.
Each replaced endpoint returns computed numbers that change with inputs (no constants).
Foreclosure on a floating individual loan returns penalty 0 (compliance check).
No NaN/Inf reachable in risk scoring for zero-history inputs.
constraints: Do not fake remediations or return placeholder numbers dressed as computed values.
Do not weaken existing auth, cooling-off, or compliance controls.
Do not rename client-facing JSON fields; only add.
Keep money in int64 paise; round float intermediates back to paise.
Line/handler references reflect current files — confirm before editing as code may have shifted.
